title:
Patterns
and Mitigation of Large Language Models’
Hallucinations on Environmental Regulatory Facts
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>With increasing adoption of large language models (LLMs) in the environmental education, research, and policy domains, reducing hallucinations─where LLMs confidently produce wrong or fabricated results─remains a critical challenge toward trustworthy agentic AI. We evaluated hallucinations on 505 environmental water, air, and solids regulatory facts collected from U.S., China, the European Union (EU), and the World Health Organization (WHO). Across four open-weight and three commercial state-of-the-art LLMs evaluated in both English and Chinese, open-weight models hallucinated on 50–70% of facts, while commercial models hallucinated on only 7–15%. We discovered a deep geographic and linguistic imbalance, where LLMs hallucinate much less on U.S. facts, and when prompting in English. Although models were less confident on average when hallucinating, a non-trivial fraction of incorrect answers were still produced with high token-level confidence. Causal tracing identified layers where restoring the subject representation most strongly recovered correct answers, with patterns differing across models. Retrieval-augmented generation effectively mitigated hallucination, even for small open-weight models. Safe deployment of AI in high-stakes environmental workflows therefore requires both targeted mitigation of training biases and robust external knowledge grounding.</jats:p>

title:
High-Throughput
Fingerprinting of Polymer Biodegradation
across Phylogenetically Diverse Microorganisms
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>With the growing accumulation of plastic waste, focus has been directed toward biodegradable polymers; however, understanding their performance across diverse microbial communities requires species-level degradation data, which throughput-limited studies of undefined or limited consortia have only partially provided, preventing the cross-species and cross-polymer comparisons driving mechanistic understanding. This work presents an integrative framework fingerprinting polymer biodegradation across phylogenetically diverse microorganisms. A modified high-throughput clear-zone assay was adapted to physiologically diverse species through minimal media formulations and used to characterize fragmentation across 19 microorganisms and 14 commercial polymers. Paucimonas lemoignei, Priestia megaterium, and Pseudomonas stutzeri showed expansive fragmentation capability. Poly(1,4-butylene adipate), degraded by 11 of 19 species, proved most universally degradable, while poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate), poly(ε-caprolactone), and poly(lactic acid) were degraded more selectively. Plate-based screening of protease, esterase, and urease activity supported the aliphatic-ester selectivity pattern. MicroResp quantification, addressing the often-conflated distinction between fragmentation and mineralization, confirmed mineralization in 63.3% (19 of 30) fragmentation-positive pairs. Comparative genomics identified 465 depolymerase homologues, 187 with predicted signal peptides. Distinct strategies─P. lemoignei’s four near-identical PhaZ paralogs versus P. stutzeri’s divergent broad-substrate α/β hydrolases─explain their comparable polyester breadth. Overall, this framework establishes a foundation for systematic accumulation of microbial biodegradation fingerprints.</jats:p>

Submarine Carbon Hydrate Storage

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Surfactant-assisted CO2 emulsion injection into cold aquifers offers enhanced CO2 storage capacity and accelerated hydrate formation. However, prior studies have largely treated surfactants as either emulsion stabilizers or hydrate kinetic promoters in isolation, leaving unresolved whether the concentration that optimizes CO2 trapping is compatible with that needed for hydrate formation near submarine temperatures. This study addresses that gap through a systematic, multiscale evaluation of SDS-stabilized CO2 emulsions. At ∼3 °C, SDS precipitates before reaching its critical micelle concentration; solubility, interfacial tension, and bulk hydrate formation experiments identify 1000 ppm as a practical upper limit for porous-medium experiments. High-pressure, low-temperature microfluidic experiments show that SDS above 500 ppm improves CO2–water displacement efficiency by increasing effective CO2-phase viscosity and reducing interfacial tension, yielding smaller CO2 ganglia and stable, piston-like displacement. SDS up to 1000 ppm shortens induction times and increases hydrate film growth rates, following a power-law dependence on subcooling with an exponent of 2. CO2 emulsions further sustain open transport pathways via continued CO2 dissolution, enabling efficient long-term CO2-to-hydrate conversion. These results define a concentration window where SDS simultaneously enhances CO2 storage and hydrate kinetics.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We examined the associations of prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) exposures with body mass index (BMI) trajectories and growth parameters in the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes Cohort. Maternal PFAS concentrations (perfluorohexanesulfonic acid [PFHxS], perfluorooctanesulfonic acid [PFOS], perfluorooctanoic acid [PFOA], perfluorononanoic acid [PFNA], perfluorodecanoic acid [PFDA], perfluoroundecanoic acid [PFUnDA], and N-methyl perfluorooctane sulfonamidoacetic acid [NMFOSAA]) were measured in serum or plasma during pregnancy. BMI trajectories and growth parameters were estimated using multiphase growth mixture modeling. Among 1,125 children ages 1–9.5 years, we identified a typical BMI trajectory (n = 998, 89%; reference group) and an atypical BMI trajectory characterized by early and rapid BMI increases (n = 127, 11%). Maternal PFOA (adjusted risk ratio [RR] = 1.22 per doubling; 95% CI = 1.05–1.41) and PFOS (adjusted RR = 1.14; 95% CI = 0.99–1.32) concentrations were associated with a higher risk of atypical trajectory membership. A doubling in maternal PFOA concentrations was associated with an earlier age at adiposity rebound by 19 (95% CI = 4–33) days. Other PFAS concentrations were not significantly associated with the atypical trajectory or adiposity rebound. In this pooled cohort study, higher prenatal exposure to certain PFAS was associated with a greater risk of an obesity-related growth trajectory and earlier adiposity rebound.</jats:p>

title:
Interaction
Between Siderite and Goethite Regulates
Fe(II) Speciation and Sustains Reduction Capacity

affiliation.name: Huazhong University of Science and Technology , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Fe(II) drives many reduction reactions in aquifers, and its reactivity is governed not merely by total abundance but also by its speciation. Siderite is a major reservoir of structural Fe(II) and frequently occurs in close proximity with goethite. But whether such close proximity effects transformation of structural Fe(II) remains unclear. This study demonstrated that coupling siderite dissolution and diffusive transport established a narrow microenvironment between siderite surface and bulk solutions, which has higher aqueous Fe(II) (Fe(II)aq) concentration and increased pH. Close proximity enables goethite to access the microenvironment and form the proton-mediated feedback interaction with siderite, promoting the formation of surface-associated Fe(II). Therefore, the surface-associated Fe(II) pool in mixed systems increased to 109.3–538.7 μM, 2.8–13.7 times higher than that in dual-chamber systems. This increase can be quantitatively predicted from siderite surface area (A) and proton activity (aH+) via a unified relationship (A·aH+0.37). The A determines the number of available reaction sites, and the aH+ governs the reaction rate. Nitrobenzene reduction experiments revealed that surface-associated Fe(II) pool sustained reduction capacity over successive reaction cycles by linking structural Fe(II) and Fe(II)aq. These findings identify interaction between siderite and goethite as an overlooked mechanism for generating a persistent surface-associated Fe(II) pool. The species distribution of Fe(II) determines the durability of abiotic natural attenuation in aquifers.</jats:p>

title:
A Supervised and
Visualization-Enabled Toolkit for
Robust DNA Reference Database Construction in eDNA Biomonitoring
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Environmental DNA (eDNA) and DNA-based technologies are increasingly used for biodiversity assessment, but their taxonomic resolution depends strongly on the quality, completeness, and interoperability of reference databases. Public barcode repositories often contain heterogeneous sequence lengths, inconsistent taxonomy, redundant records, and incomplete metadata, and existing tools do not always provide supervised curation, visual inspection, controlled database extension, and multiformat export in one workflow. Here, we present MFRefData (Multi-Format Reference Database), a Python-based toolkit for constructing customized reference databases using a paired CSV–FASTA architecture. MFRefData integrates NCBI sequence retrieval, primer-specific in silico PCR, standardized taxonomic annotation, VSEARCH-based dereplication, rule-based filtering, controlled database extension, visualization, and export to multiple commonly used compatible formats. Using the Pearl River fishes under standardized input conditions, MFRefData retrieved more sequences and covered more species than the refdb and CRABS toolkits, while also achieving higher sequence retrieval efficiency and memory efficiency. In an in silico mock community of 40 fish species and three mitochondrial 12S primer sets, MFRefData produced more correct species-level assignments than databases generated by the refdb and CRABS toolkits. Applied to real eDNA samples, MFRefData recovered broader species-level biodiversity signals. Overall, MFRefData provides a supervised, visualization-enabled, and multiformat framework for improving reference database transparency, technical quality control, and reproducibility, while supporting more reliable species-level taxonomic assignments in DNA-based biodiversity assessment.</jats:p>

title:
From
Correlation
to Causation: A Hybrid Physics-Data
Approach with Double Machine Learning for Interpretable Phosphorus
Regulation in Water Systems
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) optimization, yet black-box models often suffer from physical inconsistency and poor interpretability, causing overprediction and operational risks. This study develops a hybrid physics-data-driven framework (Phys-VMD-BiTCN-iTransformer) to enhance reliability of effluent total phosphorus (TP) prediction and control. By leveraging Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional Network (BiTCN) for spatiotemporal feature extraction, and improved Transformer (iTransformer) for long-term dependency modeling, the framework integrates operational data with seven mechanistic features derived from ASM2d and physical laws. To transition from correlation to causality, a Double Machine Learning (DML) framework was implemented. Causal inference identified Aeration Tank 1 Dissolved Oxygen (AT1 DO) and Hydrolysis Tank 1 Oxidation–Reduction Potential (HT1 ORP) as primary drivers of effluent TP fluctuations. Based on these insights, an 8-tier staged DO adjustment strategy was developed; scenario analysis showed the effluent TP compliance rate increased from 36.1% to 58.7%, while reducing exceedance risk and unnecessary energy and chemical costs. The framework bridges deep-learning architectures with practical engineering logic. By providing interpretable causal pathways and a reliable control coefficient (K = 0.15), this research offers a scalable solution for intelligent, sustainable water systems.</jats:p>

title:
Harvesting Corrosion
Energy for Self-Powered Gravity-Driven
Membrane Filtration and Fouling Regulation

affiliation.name: Xi’an University of Architecture and Technology , , ,
Xi’an University of Architecture and Technology , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Decentralized water treatment requires low-cost technologies that can remove dissolved metal ions while maintaining stable water production without external energy input. Here, we developed a soil-mediated corrosion-current hydrogel filtration system (SCHFs) that integrates a conductive adsorptive hydrogel membrane with a soil-based corrosion-energy-harvesting unit. Natural soil served as the solid electrolyte, while discarded Al and carbon cloth enabled direct harvesting of corrosion energy for conductive-membrane regulation during gravity-driven filtration. In 60-day continuous river water filtration, the SCHFs permeate concentrations of Cu2+ and Mn2+ approaching the detection limit under the tested conditions. In addition, SCHFs also accelerated NH4+-N stabilization and reduced the final permeate concentration to 0.2 mg L–1. Moreover, a thicker but more porous surface cake layer was formed during SCHF operation, limiting pore blockage and reducing the 60-day flux decline. Microbial community analysis further indicated that SCHFs reshaped the membrane biofilm and enriched taxa associated with nitrogen transformation. Soil and electrode analyses suggested that Al released from the sacrificial electrode was partly immobilized as aluminum-containing silicate minerals, suggesting a low secondary environmental risk under controlled Al input. These results suggest that coupling soil-mediated microcurrent in SCHFs regulate interfacial transport and fouling-layer architecture, thereby improving dissolved-metal retention and long-term hydraulic stability.</jats:p>

title:
Dipole Polarization
Engineering Enables Ultrahigh
One-Step Hydroxyl Radical Generation for Low-Chemical Water Decontamination
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydroxyl radicals (•OH) were key radicals for the removal of organic contaminants from water. Peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation had attracted broad interest as a route to •OH generation because of its asymmetric O–O bonds and ease of storage and transport. However, conventional Fenton-like activation of PMS typically produced •OH through a two-step pathway involving sulfate radicals (SO4•–), which incurred kinetic losses and limited •OH availability. Here, we reported a one-step •OH generation pathway from PMS enabled by synergistic polarization effects. This electronic regulation increased the O–O bond dipole moment from 0.45 to 3.86 D and produced a steady-state •OH concentration more than 2 orders of magnitude higher than those reported for representative state-of-the-art Fenton-like systems. Mechanistic analyses revealed that the amplified dipole promoted heterolytic O–O bond cleavage, thereby bypassing the SO4•– intermediate and enabling direct •OH generation. This system achieved efficient removal of diverse organic pollutants and increased rate constant of oxidant activation by 175–400% higher than the values reported for representative PMS/PDS-based Fenton-like systems. Life cycle assessment further revealed a lower environmental footprint, attributed to improved chemical utilization rates. This oxidant-centered strategy provided a promising route to utilize dipole polarization for efficient generation of •OH, with the potential to achieve scalable and low-carbon advanced oxidation water remediation.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Growing volumes of spent lithium-ion batteries challenge waste management and resource security. Conventional recycling recovers metals but often consumes energy and chemicals while sacrificing cathode structural value. Electrochemical methods enable cathode repair, controlled dissolution, and selective recovery, yet their suitability for diverse feeds and product requirements remains unclear. This Critical Review develops a material-state- and product-oriented framework linking cathode degradation, electrochemical transformations, and product specifications. Relithiation, defect repair, and cell-level rejuvenation are evaluated as regeneration strategies, with functional repurposing considered separately. Electrochemical leaching is classified by direct or indirect redox transfer, while paired or coupled operation is treated as reactor-level integration. Electrodialysis, electrosorption, and electrodeposition are assessed for ion redistribution, selective capture, concentration, and product formation. Because extraction efficiency alone cannot establish successful recycling, we emphasize feedstock tolerance, selectivity, Faradaic and ion-transport efficiencies, energy and reagent consumption, component durability, and qualified-product yield within defined system boundaries. Future priorities include diagnosis-guided routing, realistic black-mass validation, standardized reporting, scalable reactors, and integrated techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Electrochemical technologies can complement established recycling through feedstock-adaptive pathways that retain, recover, or upgrade cathode value.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bis(2-ethylhexyl)-tetrabromophthalate (TBPH), a high-production-volume novel brominated flame retardant (NBFR), has been shown to perturb thyroid hormone synthesis, yet the underlying molecular mechanism remains poorly understood. Using transcriptomics, phosphoproteomics, and metabolomics as discovery tools, combined with validation in Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats and human thyroid follicular epithelial cells (Nthy-ori 3–1), we investigated this mechanism. TBPH increased thyroglobulin (TG) and thyroid peroxidase (TPO) in rat thyroid and elevated circulating triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) levels. In Nthy-ori 3–1 cells, TBPH remodeled glycerophospholipid metabolism, leading to phosphatidylinositol synthase (PIS)-dependent accumulation of the signaling lipid lysophosphatidylinositol 18:1 (LPI_18:1). LPI 18:1 selectively activated the ERK-EGR1 signaling axis and drove TG/TPO upregulation. Knockdown of PIS or EGR1, or pharmacological inhibition of ERK, abolished TBPH-induced TG/TPO expression. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized PIS-LPI-ERK-EGR1 pathway through which TBPH enhances thyroid hormone synthesis, highlighting a lipid metabolism-driven mechanism of endocrine disruption and providing a mechanistic basis for reassessing the health risks of NBFRs.</jats:p>

Changes in Nuclear Inputs in a Baltic Sediment Core

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Anthropogenic radionuclides have been present in the environment since 1945 due to civil and military uses of nuclear energy. This study represents an extensive characterization of Am and Cm isotopes (241Am, 242mAm, 243Am, 244Cm, 245Cm, 246Cm), and 237Np, in a Baltic Sea sediment core directly impacted by discharges from the Studsvik nuclear research facility (Sweden). Distinct isotopic signatures were identified throughout the sediment core, enabling discrimination between inputs from atmospheric nuclear weapons testing (1952–1965), Sweden’s nuclear-weapons-related activities during the 1970s, and subsequent releases associated with civil nuclear-energy development. The findings demonstrate that higher actinides provide powerful isotopic fingerprints for resolving complex nuclear contamination histories and attributing release sources in environmental archives. This study further establishes the utility of actinide isotopic tracers beyond U and Pu and presents the first environmental application of the 243Am/241Am ratio in a system with well-constrained inputs from distinct nuclear sources.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nanofiltration membranes are promising for lithium recovery from salt-lake brines, yet their Mg2+/Li+ separation performance can be further improved. Here, we present an organic-phase engineering strategy that systematically tailors the carbon-chain length of alkane solvents, from n-hexane (C6) to 2-methylundecane (C12), to simultaneously regulate piperazine enrichment at the water–organic interface and trimesoyl chloride diffusion kinetics. This dual regulation transforms conventional rapid and random interfacial polymerization into a more confined and homogeneous growth process. The resulting polyamide membranes exhibit a reduced negative surface charge and a narrower and more uniform pore-size distribution. These structural features substantially enhance Mg2+/Li+ separation, with the C12 membrane achieving a Mg2+/Li+ selectivity of up to 306.6 in the mixed-salt solutions. To assess performance under realistic conditions, a two-pass nanofiltration process was evaluated using simulated salt-lake brine. The C12 membrane increased lithium purity from 2.4% to 97.7% while reducing the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio from 40 to 0.024. This study provides new insight into the kinetic regulation of interfacial polymerization through organic-phase engineering and demonstrates an effective membrane design strategy for high-selectivity lithium extraction from complex brines.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bentonite-based geotechnical barriers constitute currently an integral part of international disposal concepts of high-level radioactive waste in claystone and crystalline rock. Elevated temperature, canister corrosion, and metabolic activity of microorganisms can influence their performance. To study these effects on processes at the cast iron-bentonite interface, microcosms were incubated with two different bentonites (B27 and GMZ-001), synthetic Opalinus Clay pore water with a high water-to-bentonite ratio and cast iron plates at 37 and 70 °C over a period of 3.5 years. No microorganisms or nutrients were added to those naturally occurring in the applied materials. Cast iron surfaces in contact with GMZ-001 bentonite appeared strongly corroded, and secondary layer-like structures formed at both temperatures. Furthermore, an accelerated release of iron into the pore water, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up were observed. In contrast, incubation with B27 bentonite at 37 °C resulted in less corroded cast iron surfaces covered with iron sulfides, which seemed to passivate the surface and led to lower iron release, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up. Respective B27 microcosms were dominated by metabolically active sulfate-reducing bacteria that induced iron sulfide formation. This study shows that the corrosion behavior of cast iron and changes in geochemical parameters like pH and pore water composition depend on the applied bentonite, naturally occurring microorganisms, and temperature.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Arctic marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a key summertime source of elevated atmospheric gaseous elemental mercury (GEM), but controls on its spatial variability remain unclear. Multiscale spatial statistics, machine learning, and quantile regression were applied to MOSAiC in situ observations (June-September 2020). GEM exhibits strong fine-scale spatial autocorrelation at 10 km (Moran’s I = 0.876). Random forest model (R2 = 0.85) with SHAP attribution identified ozone (O3), chlorophyll a (Chla), and open water fraction (OWF) as dominant GEM predictors. Quantile regression revealed that nonlinear coupling among OWF, Chla, and O3 strengthens under high GEM concentrations. By further combining spatial analysis with quantile regression modeling, a GEM-sensitive region was identified (OWF = 0.156–0.404, Chla = 1.17–1.57 μg/L, O3 = 9.2–19.7 ppb); within this region, both the O3 × Chla and O3 × OWF interactions exhibited significant positive correlations. The positive effect of O3 × Chla persists across all regions, while the O3 × OWF coupling varies dynamically with the retreat of sea ice. O3 indirectly favors GEM accumulation via regulating phytoplankton, and sea-ice melt exerts stage-dependent modulation of atmospheric oxidizing capacity. This study identifies O3 as a critical MIZ mercury regulator, and embedding O3-mediated pathways in models improves GEM projections under Arctic warming.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We investigated the coastal occurrence and environmental weathering of microplastics derived from polymer-coated fertilizers (PCFs) across Japan. A field survey along the Japanese coastline revealed that PCF-derived microplastics are widely distributed on beaches throughout the country, indicating that agricultural microplastics have dispersed far beyond agricultural landscapes. Compositional analysis showed that these particles consist predominantly of polyolefins (∼70%) and polyurethanes (∼30%) and commonly exhibit oxidative degradation accompanied by iron enrichment. Bulk elemental analysis demonstrated positive correlations between iron and multiple heavy metals. Micro-X-ray fluorescence mapping using a focused 20-μm beam showed that chromium is heterogeneously distributed on the plastic surface and spatially associated with iron, while X-ray absorption spectroscopy indicated its occurrence in ferrihydrite-like phases or as chromite. Although detailed spectroscopic evidence was obtained from a single selected particle, the widespread occurrence of PCF-derived microplastics and their observed metal enrichment suggest that similar geochemical processes may occur at other coastal sites. By linking nationwide field observations with process-level characterization, this study shows that microplastics have the potential to transition from inert debris to geochemically reactive substrates after coastal deposition.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Intermittent aeration drives partial nitritation-anammox (PN-A) systems, yet how microbiomes regulate aerobic and anaerobic respiration during rapid, oxygen-limited redox shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we applied genome-resolved metatranscriptomics to evaluate transcriptional dynamics in a long-term PN-A bioreactor treating low concentrations of ammonium. Under intermittent aeration, active populations did not follow strict metabolic switching, but instead exhibited complementary regulation by coordinately transcribing aerobic and anaerobic respiratory pathways. Notably, comammox Nitrospira exhibited a severe transcriptional bottleneck, with terminal oxidase expression 2–3 orders of magnitude lower than that of amo and nirK. Gene coexpression and pathway mapping support a novel hybrid electron transport chain where electrons from ammonia oxidation are directly routed to nirK. This alternative electron-transfer route functionally couples energy dissipation with obligatory nitrite detoxification. Concurrently, a severe transcriptional deficit of nirS relative to hdh in anammox Ca. Kuenenia indicates a partial bypass of intracellular nitrite reduction. Collectively, these patterns support a novel nitric oxide-supplemented cooperation: anammox bacteria scavenge extracellular nitric oxide generated by comammox Nitrospira, conserving their own electrons while acting as a vital sink to relieve comammox nitric oxide toxicity. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for optimizing advanced PN-A microbiomes through engineered aeration control.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Coal combustion releases aromatic compound (AC) mixtures far more complex than the 16 EPA-priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Here, a high-resolution in-house database targeting 104 aromatic compounds prioritized by structural carcinogenicity alerts and structural analogy was developed to complement NIST library matching for screening fly ash, slag, and soil from five coal-fired power plants (CFPPs). This dual-database strategy increased the identification rate by 9.2% and captured 29 compounds previously unreported in the analyzed CFPP-related matrices. A total of 393 ACs spanning 24 structural classes were annotated. Cross-matrix profiling revealed distinct chemical shifts, from primary 1-ring products in slag to secondary chlorinated species in fly ash and ultimately to persistent high-molecular-weight PAHs in soils, suggesting that the observed AC patterns were associated with differences in unit efficiency, end-of-pipe control, and operational history across the five CFPPs. Incremental lifetime cancer risk assessment demonstrated that emerging PAHs contributed 60% of the total carcinogenic risk in fly ash despite comprising only ∼2% of total AC concentrations, with 4-ring compounds identified as the predominant risk drivers. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that assessments restricted to literature-derived toxic equivalency factors underestimate the full carcinogenic potential. These findings reveal a critical yet underrecognized toxic fraction in CFPP fly ash, underscoring the need for risk-oriented management strategies that explicitly incorporate emerging PAHs.</jats:p>

title: ES&T Next 60 Years: Sustainability and Climate Change

Energy
Supply and Demand Coordination Can Advance
Both Climate Goals and Sustainable Development in the Global South
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Reconciling climate mitigation with sustainable development is a critical imperative in the Global South, where rising emissions coincide with persistent development deficits. Here, we develop an integrated assessment framework linking nationally determined contribution (NDC)-aligned supply-side, demand-side, and coordinated supply–demand policy packages to greenhouse-gas trajectories and a six-goal Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) scorecard. We show that supply-focused renewable expansion or demand-focused efficiency improves selected SDG-related dimensions but creates trade-offs involving energy-cost pressure, water use, and ecosystem protection. By comparison, an integrated supply–demand strategy maximizes the SDG score (69 versus 65 under REF in 2050), enhances clean-energy penetration and efficiency, and averts approximately 485,000 annual premature deaths in 2050 relative to REF. These findings highlight the potential of coordinated supply–demand strategies to reduce climate–SDG trade-offs across the Global South.</jats:p>

title:
Divalent Cations
and Chlorine Synergistically Reshape
T6SS-Mediated Microbial Competition in Water Distribution System Biofilms
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Microbial interactions shape the community structure and function in drinking water distribution system (DWDS) biofilms, yet how the dynamic competition is regulated in biofilms remains poorly understood. Here, we show that divalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+) and chlorine in drinking water synergistically activate the type VI secretion system (T6SS) in opportunistic pathogens within biofilms. Field-collected biofilms serve as ecological hotspots that selectively enrich specific T6SS-harboring pathogens. Using simulated pipe systems and mutant validation, we further establish that divalent cations and chlorine enhance c-di-GMP signaling to promote T6SS-mediated colonization. This activation stimulates EPS production, whose polysaccharides mitigate T6SS attack, dampening the competitive advantage during mid-stage maturation but allowing gradual resurgence over extended succession. This divalent cation-chlorine-driven interplay shapes ecological succession, selectively retaining T6SS-proficient cells and establishing a “biofilm reservoir effect.” Under chlorine decay, T6SS-active pathogens can be released into bulk water, elevating exposure risks. Conversely, reducing divalent cations via nanofiltration suppresses T6SS across multiple pathogens, limiting reservoir accumulation and release. Our findings identify divalent cation availability as a key environmental signal associated with T6SS-mediated competition, linking water chemistry to pathogen persistence. This work suggests integrating membrane-based divalent cation removal with chlorine management as a chemistry-based strategy to mitigate microbial risks, advancing an integrated water quality paradigm for drinking water safety.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hexafluoropropylene oxide (HFPO)-based compounds have been increasingly adopted as replacements for legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) such as perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), yet evidence on developmental toxicity remains limited. This study investigated structure-dependent maternal-fetal transfer, fetal tissue distribution, and hepatic effects of PFOA and four HFPO-based alternatives, including hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA) and hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA) homologues, in gestational mice. All compounds were detected in maternal serum, fetal tissues, and amniotic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, but transplacental transfer efficiencies varied markedly. C9 HFPO-TA showed the greatest fetal accumulation, indicating enhanced fetal retention. Desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging revealed preferential hepatic localization of PFOA and HFPO trimers, with fetal hepatic burden increasing with van der Waals volume, suggesting structure-dependent enrichment. Metabolomics showed broad alterations of fetal hepatic metabolism, dominated by altered lipids and lipid-like molecules. 5-Aminolevulinic acid, a key heme precursor, was consistently reduced, whereas ALAS1 and ALAD protein levels increased, indicating perturbation of heme biosynthesis. The provisional, study-specific developmental reference doses derived from fetal or placental endpoints were comparable to or lower than those based on maternal hepatomegaly, suggesting greater developmental sensitivity. These findings reveal structure-dependent fetal liver accumulation and support incorporating fetal-specific endpoints into PFAS risk assessment.</jats:p>

title:

Future Nitrogen Pollution in China?

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China’s air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked the spatial heterogeneity of N-related environmental impacts and the trade-offs between reducing ammonia (NH3) emissions and N concentrations in water. This study develops a spatially explicit multiscale model system encompassing 13,000 polygons across China to assess soil N balance, NH3 emission intensity, and N concentrations in surface water, aiming to explore integrated spatial-planning (SP) strategies that maximize synergy and minimize trade-offs. Our findings reveal that single-purpose SP scenarios (e.g., reducing NH3 emissions or instream N concentrations) can effectively address one N-related issue but produce substantial trade-offs, leaving &gt;50% of China’s population exposed to at least another N-related problem. However, an integrated SP approach could reduce harmful N exposures for 90% of China’s population while ensuring food security. This approach involves reallocating 14% of livestock production, reducing livestock numbers by one-third relative to the 2050 baseline, and implementing advanced technologies to mitigate N pollution hotspots. Thus, our findings emphasize the importance of spatially explicit N boundaries and multicriteria planning to tackle N pollution in air and water simultaneously, supporting cross-media N management policy-making and region-specific strategies.</jats:p>

title: Genetic Background and Metabolic Influence on Long-Term Lithium Bioaccumulation in Mytilus Mussels and Their Hybrids

affiliation.name: Ifremer, CCEM-Unité Contamination Chimique des Écosystèmes Marins (CCEM) , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Marine mussels are widely used as sentinel organisms in coastal biomonitoring, yet the biological mechanisms controlling the bioaccumulation of emerging metals remain poorly constrained. Climate change and anthropogenic disturbances are reshaping species distributions and contact zones, promoting mussel hybridization that may alter physiological traits and contaminant-handling capacities. Lithium (Li) remains largely overlooked despite its potential toxicity and rapidly increasing global demand. Here, we investigate the influence of critical factors on Li bioaccumulation by mussels combining genetic background and isotopic approaches. Progenies of two Mytilus species and their hybrids were transplanted to the same Atlantic coastal site for 12 months. Over this in situ exposure period, Li concentrations show comparable temporal trends across all progeny groups, with an initial uptake-dominated phase followed by biodilution. Lithium isotope ratios (δ7Li) display a coherent temporal trend across all groups (decrease at early exposure, increase during later growth), and the magnitude of the shift differs slightly among genetic backgrounds. Across samples, δ7Li is coupled to growth-related metrics (dry weight) and inversely related to Li concentrations, indicating a metabolic control on Li isotope compositions of these organisms. Li concentrations are also positively correlated with lithogenic-associated elements (e.g., aluminum), consistent with the influence of particle associated Li. A simplified biodynamic modeling including Li isotopes data further indicates a more efficient Li depuration after 5 months, combined with a relatively stronger contribution from dissolved Li. Overall, growth-related factors emerged as the primary biological drivers of Li concentration and isotope variability, with the relative contributions of dissolved and particulate exposure pathways varying in association with physiological growth. Hybridization may modulate Li bioaccumulation and δ7Li values, but its influence appears secondary and does not compromise the use of Mytilus mussels as bioindicators in established frameworks such as “Mussel Watch”.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>China’s building sector is pivotal to the 2060 carbon-neutrality ambition, yet prospective assessments often insufficiently capture regional heterogeneity and life-cycle emission dynamics. Here, we develop a provincial-level dynamic framework integrating material flow analysis, life-cycle assessment, and machine-learning-informed parameter trajectories to project emissions through 2060. Under a business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, China’s building life-cycle emissions are projected to peak in 2031–2033, while carbon neutrality remains challenged by persistent pressures from both material use and building operations. These pressures arise from the existing stock, whose continued use sustains energy demand while increasing building retirements shift construction from stock growth to the replacement of retired buildings. Implementing a high-efficiency scenario with regionally differentiated deployment of material- and energy-efficiency strategies could reduce China’s building-sector life-cycle emissions by 90% in 2060 relative to the BAU scenario. Provincial analysis further reveals that similar overall mitigation potential masks substantial differences in the composition of effective mitigation portfolios, reflecting local building-stock and energy-use characteristics. To close the remaining gap, deeper operational decarbonization should be coupled with stock-management strategies that extend building lifetimes, avoid premature demolition, and prioritize renovation and reuse.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The efficiency of unconventional gas recovery is fundamentally governed by the nanoscale partitioning and competitive exchange between methane and water in shale reservoirs, yet direct experimental insight into their coupled behavior under in situ conditions (pressure and temperature) remains elusive. Here, we integrate a first-of-its-kind approach, combining contrast-matching ultra- and small-angle neutron scattering (USANS/SANS) at 50 MPa with vapor sorption, cryo-microscopy, and molecular simulations, to achieve unprecedented direct visualization of methane–water distribution across the multiscale pore–fracture network of the Longmaxi Shale. We report a fundamental revision to classical models, discovering that methane density exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on pore size, increasing with nanoconfinement but peaking sharply at ≈2 nm before declining in sub-2 nm pores. Mechanistically, water forms continuous films on hydrophilic quartz surfaces but aggregates into distinct clusters on organic kerogen. The stronger affinity of water for quartz and its increasing interaction with kerogen at higher saturations enable it to displace adsorbed methane competitively, thereby directly controlling local gas saturation. Furthermore, we reveal that microfractures are the dominant pathways for early water flowback and subsequent gas migration, with pore–fracture connectivity dictating fluid accessibility and phase exchange efficiency. These results establish a mechanistic link between interfacial nanophysics and macro-scale reservoir performance, providing a scientific foundation for optimizing hydraulic fracturing and maximizing resource recovery in deep sedimentary systems.</jats:p>

title:

Antifouling Loose Nanofiltration

Organic Wastewater Sustainable Management

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Loose nanofiltration (LNF) holds potential for sustainable management of high-salinity organic wastewater through precise organics/salts fractionation, but practical application is constrained by severe organic–inorganic combined fouling. Herein, we propose a “double-defense” antifouling strategy and develop a slippery amphiphilic LNF membrane via facile stepwise surface modification. A hydrophilic branched polyethylenimine (PEI) network was first cross-linked onto a polyamide (PA) substrate to form a fouling-resistant protection layer, followed by covalent grafting of liquid-like polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) brushes to confer a slippery, fouling-release surface. The PEI layer acts as a hydration and electrostatic barrier to repel organic-cation complexes and scale precursors, while the slippery PDMS layer with high mobility and low surface energy minimizes interfacial interactions and strengthens hydraulic shear responsiveness. During the concentration of authentic leachate membrane bioreactor (MBR) effluent, the optimized membrane showed superior antifouling performance: low flux decline ratio (FDR) of 41.6% and high flux recovery ratio (FRR) of 98.1%, outperforming a commercial PA membrane (FDR 91.2%, FRR 78.4%). It also delivered an organics/salts fractionation selectivity 7.8 times that of the commercial membrane, demonstrating multiple cycles stability. This rationally designed architecture offers a practical solution for challenging wastewater and is extensible to other PA-based membrane systems in environmental applications.</jats:p>

title:
From Nontargeted
Analysis to Toxicity: Revealing the
Disinfection Byproduct Exposome
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Chemical disinfection is essential for ensuring the microbiological safety of drinking water, but it inevitably generates disinfection byproducts (DBPs), introducing a complex and largely unresolved chemical burden. Trihalomethanes (THMs) and haloacetic acids (HAAs) have long underpinned DBP regulation, shaping monitoring and treatment strategies. However, recent analytical advances have fundamentally reshaped our understanding of DBPs. In this perspective, we examine how high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS)-based nontargeted analysis (NTA) has expanded the detectable DBP chemical space, while revealing key limitations that hinder translation from detection to identification. We then highlight emerging mass spectrometry and computational approaches as key pathways toward scalable DBP discovery and identification. We further examine the disconnect between rapid DBP discovery and limited toxicological understanding, highlighting key limitations of current toxicity assessments, including high-dose testing paradigms, fragmented end points, and overlooked mixture effects. To address these challenges, we propose an exposome-oriented framework as a conceptual model that integrates comprehensive chemical characterization with toxicity assessment, highlighting the need for future computational tools and prioritization strategies. Bridging chemical diversity to health relevance will be critical for prioritizing DBPs of concern and supporting risk-informed water quality management and public health protection.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>New particle formation (NPF) plays a critical role in atmospheric aerosol loading, yet the mechanisms controlling NPF under high-pollution conditions remain poorly understood. Ground-based measurements and GEOS-Chem-APM simulations were combined to investigate the factors governing NPF in a typical industrial city over North China Plain. During the spring campaign (3 May-2 June 2016), 10 NPF days were identified, each preceded by nighttime northwesterly ventilation and occurring under dry daytime conditions. The model reproduced 6 of 10 observed NPF events, whereas the remaining 4 showed substantially weaker simulated nucleation. Well-simulated events were generally associated with low relative humidity (RH) and condensation sink (CS) environment. NH3 remained in large excess throughout the campaign. In our test, increasing H2SO4 by up to a factor of 3 substantially enhanced nucleation rate (J) but did not fully reproduce the observed particle evolution, while replacing modeled RH and aerosol surface area with observations only moderately adjusted J. The model underestimated growth rates by 51% and 75% on well-simulated and poorly simulated days. These results indicate that nighttime ventilation reduces surface area and CS of pre-existing aerosol loading, favoring NPF, while successful reproduction of observed NPF depends jointly on diverse precursor-driven nucleation, aerosol scavenging, and subsequent particle growth.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Despite the known threats of micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) to freshwater ecosystems, their risks to zooplankton remain poorly resolved because existing evidence is fragmented across biological levels. Consequently, associations between lower-level responses and population- and community-level outcomes remain unclear. Here, we synthesized 3042 research cases from controlled experiments worldwide covering 12 response categories. We found significant overall negative effects of MNPs in systems without predators, with predators, and with predator-conditioned medium. Although molecular-level evidence remains limited, a consistent hierarchical response pattern emerged under predator-absent conditions. We therefore propose a conceptual hierarchical effect pathway (HEP) framework integrating effect sizes and cross-level associations. Within this framework, MNPs exposure was associated with increased ingestion of MNPs, physiological damage, feeding impairment, and reduced activity and defense. These responses formed an upstream tier associated with life-history impairments, including impaired growth and development, reduced reproductive capacity, and reduced survival, although these associations do not establish temporal ordering or causation. Under predator-present conditions, negative population- and community-level effects were also observed. Effect magnitudes also varied with MNPs characteristics, exposure duration, and zooplankton group. Together, the HEP framework clarifies cross-level associations and helps identify informative endpoints and incorporate food-web context into risk assessment of MNPs.</jats:p>

title:
Global
Potential
of No-Tillage in Enhancing Soil Carbon
and Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions While Sustaining Crop Yields

affiliation.name: Global Change Research Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Pursuing the balance between environmental sustainability and agricultural productivity remains a critical challenge for achieving global sustainable development goals. No-tillage (NT), as a key measure of sustainable conservation and climate-smart agriculture, offers a promising approach to addressing this challenge. However, its comprehensive effects on soil carbon accumulation, greenhouse gas emissions, and crop yields remain unquantified at the global scale, limiting our ability to optimize both environmental and agronomic outcomes. Here, we conducted such a global synthesis by combining a meta-analysis of 8,303 paired observations from 1,371 studies with a random forest model to assess the influence of site conditions and management on NT effects. Our meta-analysis demonstrates integrated benefits of NT in enhancing soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks in 0–30 cm layer by 11.0% and mitigating greenhouse gas (the sum of CO2, CH4, and N2O in CO2-equivalent) emissions by 13.5%, without a significant impact on crop yields (−0.6% ± 1.5%). The integrated benefits are stronger in drier climates and coarser-textured soils, and they exhibit significant time-dependent patterns. Our prediction identifies 44% of global croplands as being optimal for NT’s integrated benefits, mainly in Africa, South Asia, and North America. Adopting NT in these areas would result in a 4.8% increase in major food-crop yields, a 15.2% increase in 0–30 cm SOC stocks, and a 6.4% reduction in global cropland emissions, respectively. These findings underscore the relevance of implementing NT in suitable regions by adopting it into Good Agricultural Practice Guidelines.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Pollutant Release and Transfer Register (PRTR) systems in different countries are key tools for global chemicals management and an important data source for measuring progress toward achieving Sustainable Development Goal 12 of sustainable consumption and production patterns. However, current implementations face several structural and functional limitations that hinder the broad applicability of the PRTR reporting data. These limitations can be categorized into two main aspects: within-system issues and between-system inconsistencies. Within systems, data gaps can result from limited monitoring of nonpoint sources, incomplete reporting, exemptions due to thresholds and confidentiality agreements, and other similar factors, while data inaccuracies can be caused by estimation errors, duplicated counts, and other related issues. Between systems, differences in chemical lists, threshold settings, emission source types, reporting methods, and other discrepancies can hinder data comparability and integration, limiting the effectiveness of global chemicals management. Addressing these issues, through unified pollutant lists, harmonized reporting methodologies, expanded source coverage, and improved data verification, can significantly strengthen the utility of PRTR systems, advancing an integrated and evidence-based global sound management of chemicals.</jats:p>

title:
Direct Upcycling
of Rare Earth Hyperaccumulator Biomass
into Luminescent CaS:Ce Phosphors
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Rare earth elements (REEs) are essential to high-tech industries and sustainable development, but traditional mining poses significant environmental challenges. Phytomining, which uses hyperaccumulators to recover REEs from soils or low-grade mines, has emerged as a sustainable alternative; however, the high cost and low efficiency of extracting and purifying REEs from harvested biomass remain major barriers to its practical application. Here, we propose a novel in situ doping strategy to directly convert cerium (Ce)-enriched hyperaccumulator biomass into color-tunable CaS:Ce phosphors and value-added syngas, bypassing complex separation of Ca and REEs. The results show that Ce, Ca, and S could be selectively enriched from hyperaccumulator biomass to the resulting char through solvothermal pretreatment with sulfuric acid and ethanol. Subsequent steam gasification of the char produces Ce-doped CaS phosphors with broad, green-yellow emission and high photoluminescence quantum yields of 18.5–37.4%. Our approach reduces energy use by 33.6%, carbon emissions by 22.4%, and costs by \$2.62 kg–1 biomass, outperforming conventional REE recovery in both environmental and economic sustainability. This strategy provides an environmentally sustainable and economically viable route for high-value utilization of REE-rich biomass, addressing a critical bottleneck in phytomining and advancing its development as a green REE recovery technology.</jats:p>

title: Fe(II) Speciation Regulates Microbial Metabolic Reprogramming and Phototrophic Fe(II) Mineralization in Rhodopseudomonas palustris SX2
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Phototrophic iron mineralization (PIM) is a keystone biogeochemical process linking anoxic iron redox transformations to carbon sequestration. Although PIM is widely documented, how Fe(II) speciation impacts cell physiology and thus causes divergent mineralization phenotypes remains poorly understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the physiological, mineralogical, and molecular responses of a newly isolated photoferrotroph, Rhodopseudomonas palustris SX2, exposed to uncomplexed Fe(II) [Fe(II) without OM] versus organically complexed Fe(II) [Fe(II)-OM] under anoxic and illuminated conditions. We demonstrate that distinct Fe(II) speciation drives divergent metabolic reprogramming for rapid metabolic adaptation and phototrophic biomineralization phenotypes. Fe(II) without OM triggered cell-surface encrustation and activated stress-mitigation and metal-efflux systems, whereas Fe(II)-OM stimulated the formation of discrete intracellular iron nanoparticles while upregulating photosynthetic light harvesting and autotrophic CO2 fixation. Furthermore, genetic knockout and complementation confirmed that the pioABC operon constitutes the indispensable electron conduit driving Fe(II) oxidation across both speciation regimes, with organic complexation significantly enhancing its transcriptional activation. Our findings reveal how metabolic adaptation driven by Fe(II) speciation dictates the spatial distribution of biogenic iron minerals and regulates the efficiency of coupled carbon sequestration in anoxic ecosystems.</jats:p>

title:
Wastewater
Treatment Plants as Anchor Infrastructure
for Geothermal Energy in Cold Regions

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Thermal constraints in cold regions suppress biological treatment, increase energy demand, and elevate greenhouse gas emissions of existing wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), and remain a major barrier to the deployment of adequate sanitation infrastructure in many cold-region communities. Where geothermal resources exist, low-enthalpy hydrothermal heat is well matched to this energy gap. Yet, WWTPs are underrecognized anchors for broader geothermal deployment, providing a continuous, weather-independent thermal offtake through which subsurface CAPEX can be amortized. We reframe geothermal-WWTP integration as a system-level enabler that benefits both parts. Using three cascaded configurations for a full-scale WWTP, a rapid techno-economic analysis identifies three trends: energy and carbon savings/revenues alone are insufficient under realistic policy stacks, whereas crediting the upgrade-deferral value of geothermally enhanced treatment makes the project economically favorable across most policy scenarios. Globally, this triple intersection encompasses ∼11,600 catalogued WWTPs serving ∼280 million people, with a further estimate of ∼48 million people in the same regions beyond current service radii. The opportunity is greatest in cold, remote, and underserved communities, where local geothermal resources, treatment intensification, and community-scale demand together carry a case that no single driver could sustain alone.</jats:p>

title:

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Early life metal exposure has been associated with adverse neurodevelopment, with gut microbiome disruption proposed as a potential pathway. However, most studies have focused on individual taxa or pathways, despite microbes functioning within ecological communities and coordinated functional networks. Here, we integrated stool metal measurements, shotgun metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and neurodevelopmental assessments in 116 children aged 8–12 years from the GESTE birth cohort in Sherbrooke, Canada. Nineteen metals were quantified in stool samples, and neurodevelopment was assessed using parent-reported behavioral scales, attention performance testing, and resting-state fMRI. Using network-based community detection, we identified 10 co-occurring species communities (SCs) from metagenomic data and 16 coexpressed functional modules (FMs) from metatranscriptomic data and evaluated their associations with metal exposures and neurodevelopmental outcomes. Higher levels of lead, cadmium, aluminum, zinc, copper, and magnesium were associated with lower abundance of Streptococcus- and Veillonella-dominated SCs, while multiple metals were associated with lower abundance of amino acid metabolism and carbohydrate degradation FMs. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested potential indirect associations between stool metals and parent-reported ADHD-related traits througha methionine cycle-related FM or sequentially through a Clostridium spp. SC and a Factor 420 biosynthesis FM. These findings suggest that stool metal concentrations are associated with community-level variations in gut microbial composition and function, some of which were further associated with parent-reported ADHD-related traits.</jats:p>
